Night one. Walked the outer hedge of the maze until the lanterns went out. It's bigger on the inside than it has any right to be. Finley would have just run in. I'm going to count it first.
The old groundskeeper wrote everything down. Everything. Three pages on a beetle. Twelve pages on which hedges grow toward the moon. I think the second one matters. I think the first one might too.

Found the architect's blueprints under a shelf nobody dusts. The paths on paper don't match the paths in the ground. Either the architect lied or the maze moved. I've started to hope it's the architect.
A portrait on the third floor remembers the hedges being planted. She says they were planted in a spiral and then 'encouraged to disagree.' I asked what that meant. She said I'd know. I don't. Yet.
Finley asked why I keep yawning in class. I said I'd been up reading. That's true. It's not the whole truth. I've never told him half a truth before. It sits wrong.
The maze rearranges itself, but not at random. It follows the moon, like the groundskeeper said. Every turn has a reason. If you know the reason, you know the turn.

Tried a path by starlight and it held. Tried it again two nights later and it held again. I sat down in the middle of the maze and laughed until I couldn't breathe. It works. I made something that works.
I have a way through. The whole way. I've written it out three times so I can't lose it. I should tell Finley. I'm going to tell Finley. Just - after. Just once, I want to be the one who wins.
Pun, for the record, because I needed one tonight: the hedges and I have finally reached an understanding. We've agreed to stop beating around the bush.

New plans for the tournament. Every task gets a way out. Every champion gets a way home. No one walks into anything blind. Not ever again. I'll keep drawing until there's nothing left in it that could take anyone.
The new maze has exits at every turn and a light at every corner. The committee says it's too gentle. I told them gentle is the point. I think that's the loudest I've ever been.
